title: Frequently Asked Questions
questions: [{"q":"What is a Project Management Office?","a":"A PMO is a centralised function that standardises project governance, provides oversight, and supports project managers across the organisation. It can be directive, controlling, or supportive depending on organisational maturity."},{"q":"How is risk different from an issue?","a":"A risk is an uncertain future event — it may or may not occur. An issue is a risk that has materialised. Risks are managed proactively through identification and response planning. Issues require reactive resolution and must be tracked on the issues register."},{"q":"What does RACI stand for?","a":"Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed. The RACI matrix maps roles to tasks. Only one person should be Accountable for any given deliverable — this is the person who owns the outcome, not just the work."},{"q":"What is the triple constraint?","a":"The triple constraint (or iron triangle) is the relationship between scope, time, and cost. Changing any one of these affects the others. A fourth constraint — quality — is sometimes added to form the project management diamond."}]
